## Two markets, one schema.

Korean and U.S. listings are ingested and normalized every night into a single SQLite database, so an agent can read both markets’ filings and financials — and screen the Korean market — through one connection instead of two vendors.

## Primary sources only.

Filings, financials, macro series and prices are pulled straight from the issuing authority and normalized here. All of it is redistributable public data, so the licensing is clean.

### Trend and relative strength

SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger and ATR — plus an RS percentile against a name’s own market and the Minervini trend template, computed daily for every Korean listing.

### Deep financial history

Annual and quarterly financials normalized back to 2008 in the U.S. and 2014 in Korea. P/E, P/B, ROE, debt ratio and 3-year CAGR in one view. Korean price history runs from 2020, corporate-action adjusted by us. U.S. price series are deliberately not part of the product — we serve only data we may redistribute, so the licensing stays clean.

### Insider transactions

SEC Form 4 (code P buy / S sell) alongside Korean executive and major-shareholder ownership changes, split into buys and sells — the same footprints, on both markets.

### Institutional 13F holdings

“What did Berkshire add last quarter,” answered from the filing itself. Positions and value changes parsed straight out of 13F-HR.

### Filings as a news feed

U.S. 8-K and Korean material-event reports in one chronological feed. You can see what happened without paying for a news API.

### Safe direct queries

Run SELECT-only queries against the normalized database. Whitelisted and parameter-bound against injection, so the agent can compose a screen you never anticipated.

## Well-known rule sets, implemented as written.

Four publicly documented screening methods, coded as the rules are stated and run nightly over the Korean market. Every tool returns the conditions it applied and flags the parts that are approximations. We make no claims about returns.

### VCP · Trend Template

Volatility contraction plus the eight trend conditions — 200/150/50-day alignment, at least 25% above the 52-week low, within 25% of the high, and top-decile RS.

### CAN SLIM

Quarterly EPS ≥25%, annual EPS ≥25% with ROE ≥17%, near highs, sales growth, RS ≥80. The I (institutional sponsorship) and M (market direction) legs are excluded — neither can be judged from single-name data.

### Price cycle

Phase classification on the 10- and 20-day EMAs, approximating pullbacks and re-breakouts inside an uptrend. The original is discretionary, so treat this as a reference signal.

### Momentum

Moving-average alignment and short-term momentum to catch names already working. Like the Kell screen, this is flagged in the response as an approximation.

FinBridge is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any of the people or firms named above. These are our own implementations of publicly published criteria; the Kell and Schwartz screens approximate discretionary methods. Screening output is informational and is not investment advice.

## For the days you would rather not talk to a model.

The same data the MCP connector serves, as a web app. It opens the moment you sign in — nothing extra to buy, nothing to install.

### Screener · tearsheets

Strategy screens as a table; click a name for its chart, RS line, peer comparison and valuation bands on one screen.

### Portfolio · watchlist

Paste in your holdings and get one combined value across currencies plus an asset-class breakdown. Watchlists, notes and saved screens stay on your account.

### Backtests · valuation models

Run a strategy over a past window, and work DCF and RIM models by changing assumptions. The earnings calendar and seasonality sit on the same screen.

### 13F smart-money tracker

Every quarterly 13F from roughly 8,700 institutions, aggregated in full, showing what they added and what they cut. Real net buying with price appreciation stripped out, institutional consensus, new positions and exits. It opens without signing in — only the names and detailed holdings of the top three institutions and securities are withheld; ranks, dollar amounts and everything else are public.

Korean prices are adjusted for splits, mergers and capital reductions (not dividends), so indicators around dividend events can be slightly distorted. U.S. price charts, screens and backtests are not offered — U.S. coverage is filings and financials. Every screen here is informational and is not investment advice.
